title: simulationSettings.linearSolver.dropThreshold: leave out the near-zero entries of the sparse Newton Jacobian
author: Claude-JG
description: The sparse Newton Jacobian keeps every entry that is not exactly zero. In chains of rigid bodies and in contact models, 14-55 % of the nonzeros are smaller than 1e-12 times the largest entry of their row and of their column: round-off of rotations and of numerical derivatives, which cost fill-in in the factorization. A relative threshold leaves them out in GeneralMatrixEigenSparse::FinalizeMatrix, for the Newton Jacobian only; the solution is unchanged, as the residual is exact.
releaseNotes: simulationSettings.linearSolver.dropThreshold: the sparse Newton Jacobian leaves out the entries at most dropThreshold times the smaller of the largest magnitudes of their row and their column (round-off of rotations and numerical derivatives); default 0, only exact zeros; with 1e-12 a chain of rigid body spring-dampers with full Newton is 17 % faster, a chain of revolute joints 13 % slower, the results the same
